question: Should OpenClaw accept this generic durable `allowAlwaysKey` plugin approval contract now, and should Skill Workshop opt into it before its owner/audit scope is fixed?
rationale: The PR changes a public plugin approval contract and a persistent trust boundary; automation can point at the defects, but maintainers must choose the API/security shape before merge.

options.title: Fix scope before merge
options.body: Require a stable durable owner, a non-sensitive Skill Workshop scope, rebase conflict resolution, and second-call reuse proof before accepting the API.

options.title: Accept the API explicitly
options.body: Maintainers can approve the generic persistent trust contract as-is only after documenting the security model, reset behavior, and operator expectations.

options.title: Split Skill Workshop opt-in
options.body: Land a narrower generic mechanism after API review and keep Skill Workshop on one-shot approvals until its lifecycle approval evidence model is ready.

recommendation.title: Fix scope before merge
recommendation.body: Require a stable durable owner, a non-sensitive Skill Workshop scope, rebase conflict resolution, and second-call reuse proof before accepting the API.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is primarily the plugin approval API and persistent approval security contract that extends the framework history tied to this owner.
